In summary, our research is concerned with
how economic inequality is generated and how it is transmitted across generations.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a rise of economic homogeneity of couples, but that this is mainly driven by the rise in female labor force participation.
the increase in economic homogamy is not due to a change in assortative mating but rather to a change in the division of labor between spouses.
the rise of assortative mating has contributed little to the rise of inequality in the United States.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
changes in assortative mate selection have not been the main driver of economic homogamous marriages.
the increase in the division of labor in marriage has been the main driver of the growth of economic homogamous marriage.
changes in the division-of-labor mechanism, rather than the meeting and matching mechanism, are driving the rise of economic assortative mating.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rise of homogamy has been a story of women entering the labor force and men’s response to that, rather than a story of couples sorting themselves into high- and low-earning pairs.
changes in assortative matching have played a minor role in rising economic inequality.
the rise of inequality in marriage is not a result of the growing economic similarity of spouses.
